result.topic_en: Gauss computes the continued-fraction (bracket) quantities g, h, k, l, the principal points and the virtual radius (double focal length) for a thick lens whose second surface acts only as a reflector.
result.transcription:
Phys. 1
Für den Fall einer Linse deren zweite Fläche bloss reflectirt
Halbmesser (beide positiv wenn die Linse convex-convex) $r, r'$
Dicke der Linse in der Axe $c$

$u^0 = -\frac{n-1}{r}$ \quad $t' = \frac{c}{n}$
$u' = -\frac{2n}{r'}$ \quad $t'' = \frac{c}{n}$
$u'' = -\frac{n-1}{r}$

$g = (-\frac{n-1}{r}, \frac{c}{n}, -\frac{2n}{r'}, \frac{c}{n}) = 1 - \frac{2c}{r'} - \frac{2(n-1)}{n}\cdot\frac{c}{r} + \frac{2(n-1)}{n}\cdot\frac{cc}{rr'}$
$h = (\frac{c}{n}, -\frac{2n}{r'}, \frac{c}{n}) = \frac{2c}{n} - \frac{2cc}{nr'}$
$k = (-\frac{n-1}{r}, \frac{c}{n}, -\frac{2n}{r'}, \frac{c}{n}, -\frac{n-1}{r}) = -\frac{2(n-1)}{r} - \frac{2n}{r'} + \frac{4(n-1)c}{rr'} + \frac{2(n-1)^2}{n}\cdot\frac{c}{rr} - \frac{2(n-1)^2}{n}\cdot\frac{cc}{rrr'}$
$= -2\left(\frac{n-1}{r} + \frac{n}{r'} - \frac{(n-1)c}{rr'}\right)\left(1 - \frac{n-1}{n}\cdot\frac{c}{r}\right)$
$l = (\frac{c}{n}, -\frac{2n}{r'}, \frac{c}{n}, -\frac{n-1}{r}) = g$

Hauptpunkte
$\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{E}^* = \mathcal{N} + \frac{1}{\frac{n}{c} - \frac{n-1}{r}}$
Virtueller Halbmesser (oder doppelte Brennweite) $= \frac{1}{\left(\frac{n-1}{r} + \frac{n}{r'} - \frac{(n-1)c}{rr'}\right)\left(1 - \frac{n-1}{n}\cdot\frac{c}{r}\right)}$

Oder schreibt man $1 - \frac{n-1}{n}\cdot\frac{c}{r} = \lambda$
$\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{E}' = \mathcal{N} + \frac{c}{\lambda n}$
$2(\mathcal{E} - \mathcal{F}) = \frac{1}{\lambda\left(\frac{n-1}{r} + \frac{\lambda n}{r'}\right)}$

methods.what: Refraction powers and reduced thicknesses for a lens whose back surface acts as a mirror (unfolded path: refraction, reflection, refraction)
Expansion of the continued-fraction bracket g
Expansion and factorization of the bracket k (total power)
Symmetry of the system: l equals g
Location of the coincident principal points
Virtual radius (twice the focal length) of the reflecting lens
Simplified forms using the substitution λ
